prompt: Stage 5-1, level 8 with 78 gold at 40 HP, five players left. Your board is 2-star 4-costs with two 1-costs still filling slots. You are 30 XP from level 9. Put the steps of this round in the order that gets the most out of the gold.

steps: Scout: who holds the 5-costs you want and which boards are still alive to fight you
Level to 9 first (30 XP, 32 gold): it adds a slot and raises 5-cost odds before any roll is spent
Roll the remaining ~46 gold to a floor of 10, replacing the 1-costs with 5-costs or a 2-star 4-cost bruiser as they appear
Reposition against the next opponent with the new units before the timer ends

explanation:
Level before rolling, because every roll at 8 that shows a 5-cost is a roll that would have shown it more often at 9, and because the slot matters: a 5-cost you hit at level 8 can only go in by selling something. Scouting comes before both, since a 5-cost that two other players already 2-starred is one you skip in the rolldown, and knowing who you fight decides how you spend the last twenty seconds. The roll itself has a floor, because 40 HP at stage 5 is two losses and you want ten gold to rebuild from.

Repositioning is last only in sequence; it is not optional. New units in old hexes lose fights the old board would have won.
principle: Scout, level, roll, reposition: the level comes before the roll because it changes what the roll shows.
commonMistake: Rolling at 8 'to see what shows up' and then leveling with what is left, which is the same gold at worse odds with nowhere to put the hits.
